slices.focus: After a weather-service breakdown, Ayaka creates a handwritten disruption log to track notice timing, cargo handoff failures, and passenger-facing inconsistencies.
slices.summary: Ayaka describes two bad-weather sailings where passengers got inconsistent answers about medicine crates and grocery pallets. She stayed late, wrote a handwritten timeline of missed radio relays, stale whiteboard updates, and cargo-lane confusion. She got manager permission for a one-month tracking experiment with a lean five-field format and fixed status labels for cargo stages.
open_loops: One-month disruption log may not yield clear patterns
Manager's permission is informal, not policy — could be withdrawn
Risk of permanent unofficial extra workload
decisions: After a February service breakdown, Ayaka informally took on a self-started disruption log project to track notice delay
